name: Fulguris
businessModel: Open source; the Google Play build periodically prompts for a low-cost yearly subscription once a session passes twenty tabs, while the direct-download and F-Droid builds have unlimited tabs for free
basedOn: Android System WebView (fork of Lightning Browser)
paidNote: Only the Google Play build prompts for a yearly subscription after twenty tabs in a session; GitHub/direct and F-Droid builds are free with unlimited tabs
statusNote: Fork of Lightning Browser; actively released in 2026 (2.1.2 on Oct 12)
updateCadence: Irregular bursts: seven tags in Jan 2026, then 2.0.9 (Feb), 2.0.10 (Apr), 2.1.1 (Oct 1) and 2.1.2 (Oct 12)
pitch: Open-source Android browser with tab sessions, vertical tabs and heavy theming.
summary: WebView-based Android browser forked from Lightning, with named tab sessions, vertical or horizontal tab bars, force dark mode and a hosts/ABP-style ad blocker. Open source (MPL-2.0) with no sync or extensions.
bestFor: Android users with many tabs on big phones, tablets or Chromebooks
People who want themes, force dark and a bottom bar in a light browser
Open-source fans who want F-Droid builds without Firebase reporting
notFor: Anyone who needs browser extensions or cross-device sync
Users who want strong fingerprint resistance or Tor-level privacy
People who want a polished password manager

pros.title: Tab sessions
pros.detail: Named sessions let you swap whole tab sets, with vertical or horizontal tab bars like a desktop browser.

pros.title: Theming
pros.detail: Themes for the app and web pages plus force dark mode go further than most Android browsers.

pros.title: Open source, three channels
pros.detail: MPL-2.0 on GitHub, with F-Droid and direct builds that have unlimited tabs and no subscription.

pros.title: Built-in ad blocker
pros.detail: Supports hosts files and most Adblock Plus syntax from local or online lists.

pros.title: Active development
pros.detail: 2.1.1 added Android TV support and 2.1.2 improved downloads and bookmarks in Oct 2026.

cons.title: No extensions or sync
cons.detail: No WebExtensions, only userscripts, and no built-in way to sync bookmarks between devices.

cons.title: WebView limits
cons.detail: Rendering and patching depend on the device's System WebView, and features like Widevine are not provided.

cons.title: Play subscription prompt
cons.detail: The Google Play build nags for a yearly subscription after twenty tabs in a session.

cons.title: Single maintainer
cons.detail: Mostly one developer; the repo shows 313 open issues, and reviewers call the design a bit dated.

faq.q: Is Fulguris a Lightning Browser successor?
faq.a: Yes. It is a fork of Anthony Restaino's Lightning Browser, developed by Stéphane Lenclud, and adds sessions and tab bars.

faq.q: Why does the Google Play version ask for a subscription?
faq.a: The Play build shows a periodic yearly-subscription prompt after twenty tabs in a session; the F-Droid and direct builds do not.
No WebExtensions, but the F-Droid description lists userscript support.

timeline.event: Project created (slions.net lists Apr 7, 2020), forked from Lightning Browser
Seven 2.0.x releases in three weeks (2.0.3 to 2.0.8)
2.1.1 adds Android TV support (Oct 1); 2.1.2 ships Oct 12 and reaches F-Droid Oct 15

switching.note: Bookmarks with folders can be imported and exported; passwords stay with the Android autofill service.

sync.note: No sync; bookmarks can be exported

passwordManager.note: Relies on Android autofill services (one user reports a Bitwarden issue)

privacy.defaults: Incognito mode, tracking-cookie discarding and data clearing; ad blocker available
privacy.telemetry: Optional Firebase statistics and crash reports on Google Play and direct builds; none in the F-Droid build

spec.defaultSearch: Configurable (Google, Bing, Yahoo, StartPage, DuckDuckGo and custom)
spec.telemetry: Optional Firebase (Play and direct), none on F-Droid
spec.patchLag: Depends on System WebView updates on the device

android.minOs: Android 5.0 (F-Droid); tested on Android 6 to 11 per the author
notes: README also names Samsung DeX and EMUI Desktop modes and Windows 11 devices (mechanism unverified)
Android TV support with on-screen cursor since 2.1.1
README lists Chromebooks as a target

torWindows: Orbot proxy and I2P (beta), not Tor Browser
adBlocker: Hosts files and most ABP syntax
keyboardShortcuts: Keyboard support for tablets and DeX
importData: Bookmarks import and export with folders
av1: Depends on System WebView and device
downloadManager: Download and blob improvements in 2.0.10 and 2.1.2
customThemes: App and page themes plus force dark

pageLoad: WebView rendering plus optional hosts blocking
memory: Light shell; many tabs add up
battery: WebView base, ad blocker saves work
installSize: Small APK; exact size not checked
privacyDefaults: No telemetry on F-Droid; blocking is optional
blocking: Hosts and ABP-style lists, no cosmetic engine
lookCustom: Themes, force dark, tab bar layouts
extras: Orbot and I2P beta, TV mode
businessTrust: Transparent, three channels, Play nag only
